RM118.58mil | KLSE Screener \n\n## Vitrox's 3Q net profit leaps to RM118.58mil\n\n TheStar Thu, Nov 05, 2026 05:23pm - 4 days View Original \n\nKUALA LUMPUR: The business landscape is expected to remain favourable for Vitrox Bhd headed into 2027, underpinned by robust growth in the semiconductor sector, continued investment in AI data centre infrastructure and increasing demand for edge AI devices.\n\nThe group posted a bottomline of RM254.82mil in in the first nine months of 2026, nearly three times the net profit of RM87.01mil in the same period in 2025.\n\nRevenue more than doubled to RM1.13bil from RM552.73bil over the same period last year.\n\n\"This stellar cumulative performance was fundamentally supported by sustained capital expenditure deployment from strong AI infrastructure demands and electronics manufacturing customers across our main equipment segments,\" said Vitrox in its results filing with Bursa Malaysia. \n\n Summary Overview \n\n • Vitrox expects a favourable business environment into 2027, buoyed by robust semiconductor growth, expanding AI data‑centre infrastructure and rising demand for edge‑AI devices. • In the first nine months of 2026 the group posted a net profit of RM254.82 million – almost three times the RM87.01 million earned in the same period 2025 – and revenue more than doubled to RM1.13 billion; Q3 alone delivered RM118.58 million profit versus RM34.72 million a year earlier, with revenue jumping to RM485.1 million from RM228.57 million. • The surge was driven by strong demand in the Automated Board Inspection (ABI) and Machine Vision System (MVS) segments, reflecting wider adoption of advanced inspection solutions for AI infrastructure and networking equipment, underpinned by sustained capital‑expenditure from electronics‑manufacturing customers. • Vitrox will maintain prudent cost management and operational discipline to offset foreign‑exchange and geopolitical risks, while continuing heavy R&D investment RM228.57 million in Q3 2025).\n- 9M 2026 revenue: RM1.13 billion (vs RM552.73 million in 9M 2025).\n- Key drivers: strong demand in Automated Board Inspection (ABI) and Machine Vision System (MVS) The gains were driven by robust demand in Automated Board Inspection and Machine Vision System segments, fueled by broader adoption of AI infrastructure and networking equipment inspection solutions. Tax incentives from ViTrox Technologies Sdn Bhd supported earnings. The company plans continued prudent cost management and operational discipline. from RM183.0 million in the corresponding preceding quarter to RM374.9 million. This remarkable top-line performance was primarily driven by explosive Artificial Intelligence (\"AI\") infrastructure demand, our strategic focus into high-value, resilient markets like automotive, and consumer electronics and accelerated global supply chain restructuring which has deepened customer engagements. Our focus on advanced packaging and high-precision inspection solutions directly addresses the increasing complexities of AI accelerators and High Bandwidth Memory (\"HBM\") mirroring the strong momentum seen in the broader semiconductors and electronics manufacturing sector and enabling us to expand our output far beyond the previous year's low baseline. \n\n Profit before tax (\"PBT\") for the individual quarter surged by 163.7% or RM62.0 million, soaring to RM99.9 million from RM37.9 million due to structural manufacturing scale and a highly favourable product mix. Profit after tax (\"PAT\") rose by 203.9% or RM56.7 million, increasing from RM27.8 million to RM84.5 million. This bottom-line outperformance reflects exceptional operational optimization across the facilities alongside the sustained positive impact of income tax exemption enjoyed by the key subsidiary ViTrox Technologies Sdn. Bhd. All materials published here are prepared by RHB Investment Bank Bhd. For latest offers on RHB Invest trading products and news, please refer to: http://www.rhbinvest.com RHB Investment Bank Bhd Level 3A, Tower One, RHB Centre Jalan Tun Razak Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Tel : +(60) 3 9280 8888 Fax : +(60) 3 9200 2216 \n\n- Keep NEUTRAL, new MYR11.60 TP from MYR10.80, 10% upside. ViTrox Corp's 9M26 results was a beat, with yet another record quarterly earnings driven by robust AI-related demand and broad-based growth across its core businesses. We expect earnings to remain supported by a robust orderbook, favourable product mix, and progressive capacity expansion. At above peers' valuation, the slower growth potential - given the high base effect coupled with higher risk premium from the global AI outlook - leaves behind a balanced risk-reward profile.\n- Above expectations. 9M26 core earnings rose >2x to MYR253m, above our and consensus' estimates at 81% and 80%. This was driven by stronger revenue growth and margins expansion from improved operating leverage and a favourable product mix, alongside a lower effective tax rate. The stronger operating leverage lifted PBT margins to 26.5% (9M25: 20.9%). Meanwhile, the effective tax rate declined to 15.1% (9M25: 25.7%), benefiting from ViTrox Technologies' (VTSB) tax incentives, lifting earnings margins to 22.6% (9M25: 25.7%).\n- Sequential net profit growth continues. 3Q26 revenue rose 29.4% QoQ to MYR485.1m, driven by stronger shipment fulfilment across the automated board inspection (ABI) and machine vision system (MVS) segments, supported by sustained demand for AI infrastructure and networking equipment. The stronger topline, coupled with operating leverage and favourable product mix, lifted PBT by 36.8% QoQ to MYR137m, with PBT margin expanding 1.5ppts to 28.2%. Consequently, core profit increased 56.8% QoQ to MYR118m (2Q26: MYR75m), further supported by a lower effective tax rate of 13.7% (2Q26: 15.5%).\n- Positive outlook. We expect earnings momentum to remain robust into FY27, underpinned by sustained AI-related demand and a healthy order pipeline, with incoming orders continuing to outpace shipment capacity. Planned capacity additions should progressively unlock the order backlog from 4Q26 onwards, accelerating shipment conversion and easing the record high book-to-bill ratio. Campus 5.0 (completion targeted by FY28) should drive another step-up in capacity, while renewed pioneer tax incentives provide further earnings tailwinds from FY27 onwards, in our view.\n- Earnings and TP. We raise our FY26F-28F earnings by 14%, 8%, and 7% to reflect stronger-than-expected order conversions as shipment volumes ramp up. We expect a favourable product mix, operating leverage, and continued pioneer tax incentives to support earnings growth into FY27. We raise our TP to MYR11.60, pegged to an unchanged 50x (+1.5SD) FY27F P/E. At 46x FY27F P/E, ViTrox's valuation already factors in substantial earnings growth, leaving limited headroom for further re-rating given the slower growth and higher risk premium outlook. Key risks: A slowdown in AI/hyperscaler capex or a broader semiconduction down-cycle, component shortages and capex delays, and margins pressure from Chinese competition and FX. The opposite represents the upside risks.\n\nSource: RHB Research - 6 Nov 2026\n\n Be the first to like this.
